text.p: Quintiles Transnational Corp said Wednesday it has signed a definitive agreement to buy BRI International Inc, a global contract research organization based in Arlington, Va.

The acquisition would be slightly accretive to Quintiles' 1996 fourth quarter earnings per share, excluding a one-time charge of about $4.8 million related to the transaction, Quintiles said. Earnings could add up to 5 cents per share in 1997, the company added.

Quintiles said the agreement calls for an exchange of 100 percent of BRI stock for about 1.9 million shares of Quintiles stock. It said the acquisition is subject to BRI shareholder approval and regulatory approval, and that completion is expected later this year.

The transaction is expected to be accounted for as a pooling of interests, the company added. Quintiles said it will enter into employment agreements with certain BRI employees, including BRI chairman and chief scientific officer Frank Hurley.
The acquisition "significantly expands our ability to meet the global needs of the pharmaceutical, biomedical and medical device industries," Quintiles Chief Executive Dennis Gillings said.
BRI is a contract research organization serving the pharmaceutical, biotechnology and medical device industries out of offices in the United States and Europe.
Quintiles provides research, development and consulting services to pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device and healthcare management industries, as well as local and national governments.
